topic.title: Logarithmic Expressions
topic.summary: What log_b c means, evaluating logarithms with and without technology, the common logarithm, and logarithmic scales.

lesson.title: Logarithmic Expressions
lesson.summary: What log_b c means, evaluating logarithms with and without technology, the common logarithm, and logarithmic scales.
lesson.bigIdea: A logarithm answers one question: what exponent turns the base into this number? Every logarithm statement is an exponential statement read the other way.
lesson.context: Topics 2.3 to 2.5 asked for outputs of exponential functions. Logarithms ask for the input instead, which is the step needed to solve exponential equations and to build logarithmic functions in Topic 2.10.

sections.title: 2.9.A · log_b c is the exponent that b must be raised to in order to obtain c.

blocks.text: The logarithmic expression log_b c is equal to, or represents, the value that the base b must be exponentially raised to in order to obtain the value c. That is, log_b c = a if and only if bᵃ = c, where a and c are constants, b > 0, and b ≠ 1. (when the base of a logarithmic expression is not specified, it is understood as the common logarithm with a base of 10)

blocks.caption: Each logarithm statement is an exponential statement
rows: 2 must be raised to 5 to obtain 32.
3 must be raised to −3 to obtain 1/27.
A unit-fraction exponent is a root.

blocks.title: Write it like the AP Exam
blocks.text: log₄ 64 = 3 because 4³ = 64. State the exponential form as the reason.

sections.takeaway: log_b c = a means bᵃ = c. No base written means base 10.

sections.title: 2.9.A · Some logarithms are exact; others are estimated with technology.

blocks.text: The values of some logarithmic expressions are readily accessible through basic arithmetic while other values can be estimated through the use of technology.
log₅ 125 = 3 is exact, because 125 = 5³. log 40 is not an integer: since 10¹ = 10 and 10² = 100, log 40 is between 1 and 2, and technology gives log 40 ≈ 1.602.
When the argument can be written as a power of a common base, rewrite both: log₈ 4 asks for a with 8ᵃ = 4. Since 8 = 2³ and 4 = 2², (2³)ᵃ = 2², so 3a = 2 and log₈ 4 = 2/3.

blocks.title: Write it like the AP Exam
blocks.text: On the no-calculator Question 4, find exact values such as log₂ 8 = 3. Use a decimal only when a calculator is allowed and the value is not exact.

sections.takeaway: Rewrite as powers of a common base for exact values; estimate the rest with technology.

sections.title: 2.9.A · On a logarithmic scale, each unit is a multiplicative change.

blocks.text: On a logarithmic scale, each unit represents a multiplicative change of the base of the logarithm. For example, on a standard scale, the units might be 0, 1, 2, …, while on a logarithmic scale, using logarithm base 10, the units might be 10⁰, 10¹, 10², ….

blocks.caption: Equal steps on a base-10 logarithmic scale

blocks.text: Moving one unit to the right multiplies the value by 10, so values that differ by many orders of magnitude, such as the intensity of a whisper and a jet engine, fit on one scale.

sections.takeaway: Equal steps on a log scale mean equal factors, not equal differences.

connections.title: Unit-fraction exponents
connections.body: Topic 2.4 showed that b^(1/k) is the kth root of b. That is why log₉ 3 = 1/2 and log₈ 2 = 1/3.

connections.title: Logarithmic functions
connections.body: Topic 2.10 turns log_b x into a function of x and shows it is the inverse of the exponential function bˣ.
